notes: Texting mode now actually means texting. Characters kept narrating themselves in asterisks in chats that were supposed to be plain messages, and the reason was mostly the history: switching a conversation to texting leaves every earlier in-person message sitting there in asterisks, which reads to the model as a worked example of exactly the thing it was told not to do. Three changes. The instruction is blunt now — you are on your phone, they are on theirs, you cannot see each other, so type what you would type and nothing else. It is repeated as the last thing before the reply, with the history explicitly disowned, the same trick that fixed replies ignoring the length setting. And it no longer relies on the model agreeing: actions in asterisks are cut from the reply on the way to the screen, mid-stream as well, so a half-typed one never flashes up. A single word in asterisks survives as plain text, because people really do type it that way for emphasis, and a reply that was nothing but narration is left alone rather than sent as an empty bubble — that case gets logged instead. In-person mode is untouched: there the asterisks are the whole point.
